articles.title: Improving prostate MRI quality assessment across diverse evaluators and institutional practice through a PI-QUAL v2 lecture: a pilot study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of a prostate imaging quality (PI-QUAL) v2 lecture on the accuracy and inter-reader agreement of prostate MRI image-quality assessment among radiologists and technologists from diverse professional backgrounds and institutions, and to evaluate its role in institutional-level quality improvement through a quality control (QC) process. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Ten participants (five radiologists and five technologists) from five different hospitals independently evaluated 15 prostate MRIs before and after a standardized PI-QUAL v2 lecture. Reference scores were established by two experienced radiologists. Concordance with reference was assessed using accuracy and balanced accuracy. Inter-reader agreement was measured using percent agreement (PA) and Gwet's AC1. Subgroup analyses were conducted based on participant characteristics. For the quality assurance and QC (QA/QC), each center submitted 15 prostate MRIs before and after the lecture. Image quality was evaluated centrally to assess institutional improvement. RESULTS: Overall accuracy increased from 66.7% to 76.7%, and balanced accuracy increased from 62.9% to 84.2%; the mixed-effects model indicated significantly higher post-lecture accuracy (p = 0.038). Accuracy was also higher across all subgroups. Inter-reader agreement improved from PA 57.6% to 72.6% and Gwet's AC1 from 0.214 to 0.466. Through the QA/QC process, three centers initially failed to meet PI-QUAL v2 technical criteria. After feedback, all post-intervention scans achieved PI-QUAL v2 scores > 1. CONCLUSION: A structured PI-QUAL v2 lecture improved both the accuracy and inter-reader agreement of prostate MRI image-quality assessments among diverse evaluators. Incorporating QA/QC further enhanced institutional image quality. PI-QUAL v2 training is a feasible strategy for standardizing prostate MRI quality. KEY POINTS: Question Does a structured PI-QUAL v2 lecture for radiologists and technologists improve prostate MRI quality assessment performance and institutional imaging practice across institutions? Findings PI-QUAL v2 training improved accuracy (66.7% to 76.7%) and inter-reader agreement in prostate MRI quality assessment, while QA/QC feedback enhanced institutional imaging quality. Clinical relevance statement Structured PI-QUAL v2 education combined with quality assurance and quality control feedback improves evaluator consistency and institutional prostate MRI quality, facilitating standardized image-quality assessment and broader implementation of high-quality prostate MRI in clinical radiology.

articles.title: A multicentre immersive virtual-world course for radiology residents: feasibility, educational outcomes, and participant perceptions.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To design and implement an immersive course on plain radiograph interpretation for radiology residents within a three-dimensional virtual world and to evaluate its feasibility, participants' perceptions, and short-term changes in knowledge-test performance. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The course, delivered in a three-dimensional virtual world over 22 days, included seven 3-h synchronous sessions and asynchronous case-based activities. Educational outcomes were assessed using pre- and post-course multiple-choice tests. Participants' experience was evaluated using 9-point Likert-scale items assessing cognitive load, perceived course level, and usefulness for clinical practice. After the course, participants completed an evaluation questionnaire including 5-point Likert-scale items, numerical ratings (0-10), and open-ended questions. Student's t-test was used for continuous variables and the Mann-Whitney U test for ordinal data. RESULTS: Sixty-seven residents from 27 hospitals met the certification criterion across two editions in 2021 and 2022. Forty-seven completed both the pre- and post-course tests, with mean scores increasing from 60.4 ± 6.5% to 70.2 ± 9.0% (p < 0.001). Participants reported positive perceptions, with high agreement for usefulness and adequacy (> 90%) and a mean usefulness score of 7.7 ± 1.2. Ratings were generally high (> 7/10), particularly for instructors, educational content, and course organisation, whereas interaction among participants received lower ratings. CONCLUSIONS: Immersive online teaching in a three-dimensional virtual world is a feasible approach for radiology resident education. Participation in the course was associated with improved short-term performance on a repeated knowledge test and positive participant perceptions. This format may complement traditional teaching methods in cohorts composed predominantly of early-year radiology residents. KEY POINTS: Question Flexible educational approaches are needed to reinforce plain radiograph interpretation training among radiology residents, but evidence supporting virtual-world training remains limited. Findings The virtual-world course was feasible and positively valued by participants, with participation associated with improved short-term performance on a repeated knowledge test. Critical relevance statement Immersive teaching in a three-dimensional virtual world is a feasible and well-accepted approach that may complement plain radiograph interpretation training in cohorts composed predominantly of first and second-year radiology residents.

articles.title: Ghost cell odontogenic carcinoma: a case report and literature review.
articles.abstract: Ghost cell odontogenic carcinoma (GCOC) is an exceedingly rare malignant odontogenic epithelial tumor, distinguished by the presence of ghost cells. GCOC exhibits nonspecific clinical and radiologic features, such as variable pain, swelling, and osteolytic destruction without distinct periosteal reaction, and can be locally destructive and invasive, with the potential for distant metastases. Currently, no effective systemic therapy is recommended for patients. We present a case of a 56-year-old male patient diagnosed with GCOC involving the maxilla, along with a review of the previous literature. The patient underwent en bloc resection of the tumor. However, the tumor recurred 3 months later, and the patient opted for conservative management. Unfortunately, the patient passed away 2 weeks after the recurrence. Based on the case presentation and literature review, we conclude that GCOC represents an aggressive malignancy with a high potential for local recurrence and metastatic disease. This necessitates preoperative accurate imaging diagnosis to guide radical resection, and highlights the need for effective adjuvant therapies, which are currently unavailable, to prevent rapid disease progression and mortality.

articles.title: Can Spleen T1 Mapping Be Used as a Marker of Adenosine Response in Cardiac MRI?
articles.abstract: Splenic switch-off, defined as the visible reduction in splenic perfusion during adenosine stress, can be used as a marker of adequate adenosine response in cardiac stress MRI studies, which can be assessed after the study. Moreover, there is some evidence regarding the use of T1 mapping for the evaluation of splenic switch-off during the study. The aim of this work is to further investigate splenic T1 mapping as a method for quantitatively assessing splenic switch-off, given the limited existing data. Patients with suspected coronary artery disease were scanned at 1.5 T with the routine clinical protocol for stress perfusion cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), including a T1 mapping sequence at rest and during adenosine stress. Visual assessment of first-pass images was used as the reference standard for detecting splenic switch-off. Semi-quantitative analysis of splenic perfusion was performed based on the signal intensity curves and signal changes (ΔSI) were calculated. T1 maps were used to obtain T1 value changes in the spleen from rest to stress (ΔT1spleen). Statistical analysis was assessed using an align rank transform followed by a mixed analysis of variance, with Bonferroni corrected post hoc tests. A total of 74.5% (n = 35/47) of analyzed patients experienced splenic switch-off according to the visual assessment. Statistically significant differences were found in splenic T1 between rest and stress only in the switch-off group (p < 0.001), with lower T1 values during stress. There was significant positive weak correlation (ρs = 0.37, p = 0.01) between splenic ΔT1 and ΔSI based on first-pass. ROC curves demonstrated that ΔT1spleen classified the failed switch-off and positive switch-off groups with a specificity of 75% and a sensitivity of 80% (AUC: 81.2%, 95% CI: 66.7%-95.8%). This work indicates that the splenic T1 value change has the potential to identify splenic switch-off during adenosine stress CMR in a clinical population.

articles.title: Liver Viscosity Dominates Liver Stiffness in MASLD: A Multiparametric Ultrasound Study With IPTW Adjustment and Explainable Machine Learning.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Liver stiffness measured by shear wave elastography (SWE) is widely used as a noninvasive surrogate for fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). However, stiffness may be influenced by multiple biomechanical factors beyond fibrosis, and the relative contributions of inflammation-related viscosity, steatosis, and metabolic parameters remain unclear. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective study, 573 adults with MASLD underwent multiparametric ultrasound, including SWE, viscosity plane-wave ultrasound (ViPLUS), and attenuation (ATT). Participants were stratified into lower-body mass index (BMI) (BMI < 24 kg/m²) and higher-BMI (BMI ≥ 24 kg/m²) groups. Covariate balance was achieved using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). Multivariable linear regression, subgroup analyses, and interaction testing were performed to identify independent determinants of liver stiffness. Machine learning models (extreme gradient boosting [XGBoost]) with Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) were used for exploratory feature attribution to identify key determinants of liver stiffness rather than to develop a standalone clinical diagnostic or prediction tool. RESULTS: After IPTW adjustment, prespecified clinical covariates were well balanced between BMI groups. Hepatic viscosity (ViPLUS) was the strongest independent determinant of liver stiffness (β = 5.80, 95% confidence interval: 5.33-6.27; p < 0.001), corresponding to an approximately 0.58 kPa increase in SWE per 0.1 Pa·s increase in ViPLUS. The association remained dominant in both BMI groups and was greater in the higher-BMI group (approximately 0.63 vs. 0.51 kPa per 0.1 Pa·s). The contribution of viscosity was consistently dominant across lower-BMI and higher-BMI subgroups and appeared stronger in the higher-BMI group. SHAP-based feature attribution identified ViPLUS as the most influential model-derived feature associated with SWE, consistent with the regression findings. Nonlinear associations were observed for aspartate aminotransferase/alanine aminotransferase ratio and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, while triglycerides and glucose showed no significant nonlinear relationships. Notably, a subset of lower-BMI individuals exhibited high-risk hepatic phenotypes despite lower BMI. CONCLUSION: Hepatic viscosity is the dominant determinant of liver stiffness in MASLD, with even a 0.1 Pa·s increase in ViPLUS corresponding to an approximately 0.58 kPa increase in SWE. These findings suggest that liver stiffness reflects viscosity-related viscoelastic alterations rather than fibrosis alone. Multiparametric ultrasound, particularly the integration of viscosity and stiffness, may provide incremental value for identifying high-risk individuals, including those with lower BMI.

articles.title: Development of Entrustable Professional Activities for Core Diagnostic Radiology Procedures: An APDIR Workgroup Initiative.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Although entrustable professional activities (EPAs) have been adopted across many medical specialties, their use in radiology remains limited, largely to subspecialty areas such as breast imaging. A standardized set of EPAs for procedural training in diagnostic radiology has not been widely available. We sought to develop EPAs for 10 core diagnostic radiology procedures through a structured, consensus-based process, providing programs with a behaviorally anchored framework for assessing procedural competence. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using a consensus-based, expert-panel approach with iterative refinement, a volunteer panel of nine integrated interventional radiology (IR) residency program directors from nine distinct academic institutions adapted the American Board of Surgery's general surgery EPA framework as a template. Ten core diagnostic radiology procedures, previously identified by a joint task force of the Association of Program Directors in Radiology and the Association of Program Directors in Interventional Radiology, were selected for development. Subject-matter experts drafted an EPA for each, a single author harmonized them, and the full panel reviewed and approved the final versions. RESULTS: Ten EPAs were developed, one for each of the core diagnostic radiology procedures. Each EPA describes the procedure-specific behaviors expected at each phase of care across four entrustment levels-Limited Participation, Direct Supervision, Indirect Supervision, and Practice-Ready. A completed example is provided in Table 1. CONCLUSION: A shared set of procedural EPAs for diagnostic radiology was developed through a structured, consensus-based process built on an established general surgery framework. These EPAs give programs a practical way to assess procedural competence and to support decisions about the level of supervision a resident requires for a given procedure.

articles.title: Percutaneous Recanalization of Chronic Noncirrhotic Native-Liver Extrahepatic Portal Vein Obstruction in Children.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate technical success, procedure-related safety, and imaging-based patency of percutaneous portal vein recanalization (PVR) in children with chronic native-liver extrahepatic portal vein obstruction (EHPVO). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 28 consecutive patients younger than 17 years with chronic noncirrhotic, nonmalignant EHPVO who underwent attempted PVR between 2016 and 2026. Recanalization was performed through transhepatic, transsplenic, or combined access, followed by balloon angioplasty without stenting. Technical success was defined as restoration of hepatopetal flow through the portal vein into the intrahepatic portal venous system. Adverse events were graded using the Society of Interventional Radiology classification. Portal vein patency was assessed on available follow-up imaging. RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in 19 of 28 patients (67.9%). Six patients (21.4%) had access-related adverse events (3 mild, 1 moderate, 2 severe), with no surgery, permanent sequelae, or procedure-related death. Follow-up imaging was available for 15 of 19 technically successful patients, with a median imaging follow-up of 11 months (range, 1-35 months). At last imaging, the portal vein was patent without significant restenosis in 7 patients, patent with restenosis in 5, and reoccluded in 3. Overall, portal venous flow was maintained in 12 of 15 patients (80.0%). CONCLUSION: Percutaneous PVR restored hepatopetal portal flow in 67.9% of selected children without stenting. Durable patency could not be established because follow-up was incomplete and heterogeneous. Restenosis and reocclusion support structured imaging surveillance; further studies should define the role of stenting versus angioplasty alone.

articles.title: A Branch-Specific Combined Fenestration Strategy for Chronic Aortic Dissection With Severe Paravisceral True Lumen Compression.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate a branch-specific combined fenestration strategy to address the technical challenges of severe true lumen (TL) compression during physician-modified fenestration (PMF)-based four-vessel visceral reconstruction in chronic aortic dissection (CAD). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled twenty-three consecutive patients with aneurysmal CAD and severe paravisceral TL compression (minimum functional TL diameter ≤10 mm) treated between January 2020 and December 2024. All patients underwent visceral reconstruction using anterior-branch PMF and bilateral renal in situ laser fenestration (ISLF) performed following TL expansion. Endpoints included technical success (complete four-vessel reconstruction), 30-day mortality, target-vessel patency, and TL expansion. RESULTS: Complete four-vessel visceral reconstruction was achieved in all 23 patients (92/92 target vessels). Renal ISLF was successful in all 46 renal arteries, with first-attempt success in 44 (96%). Distal aortic exclusion was required in 20 patients; one interval infrarenal rupture in the staged group was managed with emergency repair. Over a median follow-up of 17.0 months, primary target-vessel patency was 99% (91/92). The median minimum functional TL diameter increased from 8.0 mm preoperatively to 15.9 mm at one-year follow-up. No type I or III endoleak was identified. Thirty-day mortality was 0%. Transient spinal cord ischaemia occurred in one patient (4%), and acute kidney injury (KDIGO Stage 1) in two patients (9%), all resolving before discharge. CONCLUSION: In highly selected CAD patients with severe TL compression, this combined fenestration strategy enabled complete four-vessel visceral reconstruction with satisfactory early target-vessel patency and no target-vessel loss, though longer follow-up in larger cohorts is required.

articles.title: Does Phubbing Always Elicit Social Pain? The Role of Belonging Context.
articles.abstract: Phubbing, a prevalent interpersonal phenomenon in which individuals divert their attention to their phones while neglecting their interaction partners during face-to-face interactions, has been associated with adverse psychological and relational outcomes, including social pain. However, the same "eyes-on-phone" behavior may not always be experienced as phubbing or evoke feelings of neglect and social pain. The present research examined whether belonging context shapes behavioral and neural responses to "eyes-on-phone" behavior during face-to-face interaction. In Study 1, 163 participants completed a scenario-based task that required them to judge how they felt about several stories, in which belonging context (positive, negative, unrelated) was crossed with attentional state (eyes-on-phone, eyes-on-you). In Study 2, 50 participants completed the Cyberball paradigm to manipulate different belonging contexts (positive, negative, unrelated) with 6 models, followed by an ERP experiment in which they judged whether images of these models displaying different attentional states (eyes-on-phone, eyes-on-you) made them feel neglect-related social pain. Across both studies, within "positive" contexts, "eyes-on-phone" behavior elicited greater social pain, including perceived neglect, emotional unpleasantness, and unwillingness to communicate (Study 1), as well as a greater tendency to endorse neglect-related social pain and larger P3 amplitudes (Study 2) than "eyes-on-you" behavior, whereas this pattern was not consistently observed in the "negative" or "unrelated" contexts. These findings indicate that phubbing is not inherently experienced as social pain. Rather, its social meaning depends on prior belonging context: a mismatch between contextual cues and subsequent attentional behavior may give rise to expectancy violations, which could contribute to social pain when the behavior is interpreted as neglectful.

articles.title: Learning Dynamic Affinity Diffusion for Multi-Contrast MRI Super-Resolution via Implicit Neural Representations.
articles.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) super-resolution (SR) focuses on reconstructing high-quality, high-resolution target images from sparsely acquired signals while enhancing reconstruction performance through guidance from a reference image. In clinical practice, MRI SR contributes to reduced scan durations and alleviates patient discomfort, as well as motion artifacts associated with extended immobility. Existing SR approaches, however, exhibit insufficient interaction with texture features from the reference image, which results in pronounced inaccuracies at image edges. In addition, these methods often neglect the issue of noise amplification introduced during the SR process. To overcome these limitations, an implicit dynamic spatial propagation network (IDSPN) is introduced, integrating an implicit neural network with dynamic spatial propagation. Initially, residual dense blocks and residual channel attention networks are employed to extract features from the low-resolution input and reference images, respectively. Subsequently, a texture transformer performs feature alignment between the input and reference images and transfers texture information from the reference image to the low-resolution input, followed by upsampling through an implicit neural network. A backbone network then estimates affinity and propagation offsets, enabling refinement via multi-stage iterative diffusion. The proposed approach is evaluated on three publicly available datasets, with experimental findings demonstrating state-of-the-art performance and indicating its potential for clinical application. Codes are available from https://github.com/whj-proj/IDSPN.git.

articles.title: Experimental feasibility study of proton therapy range verification by a digital tracking calorimeter prototype.
articles.abstract: Objective.Uncertainties in the proton range remain an important challenge in proton therapy. In-situ range verification techniques can be used to ensure the Bragg peak depth in the patient matches the treatment plan. Various such methods are under investigation, utilizing the signal from secondary radiation caused by proton interactions with the patient. This study experimentally investigates the feasibility of using a silicon-pixel-based sampling calorimeter for range verification through the detection of secondary photons and neutrons.Approach.The proton range verification capability of a sampling calorimeter based on monolithic active pixel sensors was tested both theoretically and experimentally. We theoretically investigate the plausibility of the planned sampling calorimeter to pick up a signal from the neutral secondary particles distal to the patient. Then, a smaller prototype pixel telescope was constructed to verify our theoretical findings experimentally by placing it behind a water tank irradiated by a medical proton beam with various energies in the range of 100-200 MeV at the Danish Centre for Particle Therapy, Aarhus, Denmark.Main results.We find that the aluminum used as absorbers between sensitive layers in the calorimeter serves as a converter for prompt gammas and neutrons. The combined detection efficiency ranges between 5.8·10-5and 2.7·10-3detector hits per primary proton for beam energies between 50 and 200 MeV. Irradiation of the water phantom leads to a signal in our detector, which is well-correlated with the nominal beam energy. A simulation-based model using only the number of hits per proton can predict the beam energy, acting as a proxy for proton range in a homogeneous target, down to a root mean squared error of 1.34 MeV.Significance.This study marks a promising step towards utilizing a tracking calorimeter designed for proton computed tomography for the secondary application of proton therapy range verification without additional hardware costs.

articles.title: SalientNet: mechanistic and reliable saliency maps for medical image classification via unsupervised learning.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Interpreting neural network decisions is crucial in healthcare, where both global and local validations are essential for building trust. While saliency maps offer intuitive visualizations of model attention, their limitations-including low sensitivity to input perturbations, lack of causal grounding, and limited mechanistic insight-reduce their reliability in critical medical scenarios. This study aims to develop a more trustworthy and mechanistically interpretable framework for explaining convolutional neural network (CNN) decisions in medical image classification. METHODS: We propose SalientNet, a data- and architecture-agnostic unsupervised neural network framework for interpreting CNNs. SalientNet consists of two jointly trained components: a CNN examiner, which uses a novel variable channel convolution (VCC) module to extract architecture-independent information from a CNN's intermediate feature maps, and an attribution map generator, built from two coupled U-Nets, which combines this information with the input image to produce a saliency map. Training requires no ground-truth saliency annotations; instead, an Interpretation Loss enforces that the attribution map retains just enough information for a frozen classifier to reproduce its original prediction within a controlled tolerance (dissimilarity temperature), preventing both trivial and overly aggressive masks. We evaluated SalientNet on three medical imaging datasets spanning different modalities and body regions-BreakHis (histopathology), Brain MRI ND5, and FracAtlas (musculoskeletal X-rays)-using ResNet-18, MobileNetV3-Small, and EfficientNet-B0 as the interpreted classifiers. RESULTS: Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that SalientNet outperforms popular saliency-based benchmarks, including Grad-CAM, Grad-CAM++, and LIME, achieving substantially higher faithfulness (Win %) and lower prediction Drop (%) across nearly all dataset-architecture combinations, while keeping spurious confidence increases (Inc %) comparably low. On FracAtlas, SalientNet's explanations also showed strong spatial correlation with fracture regions annotated by medical practitioners, with a mean ground-truth active fraction of up to 0.96 for ResNet-18. A mechanistic analysis further shows that nearly all CNN layers contribute meaningfully to SalientNet's explanations, supporting its interpretive fidelity. CONCLUSION: Our unsupervised framework provides improved interpretability for CNNs in healthcare applications, offering a more reliable and mechanistically grounded alternative to traditional saliency methods for local validation and building trust in AI-assisted medical diagnosis. Our implementation is publicly available https://github.com/S-iddhaarth/Unsupervised-Training-of-an-Interpretable-Neural-Network-to-Explain-Convolutional-Neural-Networks here.

articles.title: CT-based deep learning integrating pancreatic imaging and body composition for severity prediction in acute pancreatitis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate a deep learning (DL)-based CT model integrating pancreatic imaging and CT-derived body composition for severity prediction in acute pancreatitis (AP). MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective dual-center study, patients with AP who underwent CT within 72 h of symptom onset were enrolled from January 2021 to September 2025 at Center 1 and January 2023 to September 2024 at Center 2. The primary dataset (n = 426) was randomly divided into a training set (n = 298) and an internal test set (n = 128), while 110 patients from Center 2 served as the external test set. A three-dimensional DL model was developed for pancreatic imaging, and two-dimensional DL models were constructed for L3-level visceral adipose tissue (VAT) and skeletal muscle (SM). Six predictive models were constructed: clinical, pancreas, VAT, SM, pancreas-clinical (PC), and combined. Performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis, DeLong testing, calibration, decision curve analysis, net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). RESULTS: The combined model achieved area under the curve (AUCs) of 0.897 (95% CI: 0.862-0.932), 0.909 (95% CI: 0.861-0.958), and 0.910 (95% CI: 0.856-0.964) in the training, internal test, and external test sets, respectively. The combined model outperformed the PC model in the training set (p = 0.002) and external test set (p = 0.020). NRI and IDI analyses confirmed the incremental predictive value of body composition features. CONCLUSIONS: A CT-based DL model integrating pancreatic imaging, body composition, and clinical variables demonstrated good performance for AP severity prediction. KEY POINTS: Question Early severity stratification in AP remains challenging because conventional clinical and imaging assessments may not fully capture pancreatic injury and systemic disease status. Findings A CT-based DL model integrating pancreatic imaging, body composition, and clinical variables demonstrated good performance for severity prediction in AP. Critical Relevance Statement This study evaluates the value of integrating pancreatic imaging and CT-derived body composition information and supports the use of routinely acquired CT data for early risk stratification, potentially facilitating more individualized monitoring and management of AP.

articles.title: Serial MRI of spontaneous spinal epidural hematoma in infancy managed conservatively: a case report.
articles.abstract: We present a case report on the conservative treatment of spontaneous spinal epidural hematomas (SSEHs) in infancy, a very rare condition. Physical examinations and serial MRIs were conducted for SSEHs located between C7 and T4. About 4 months after the onset of the first symptoms, normal muscle strength was observed in the lower limbs of the patient who had experienced bilateral lower limb paralysis, and MRI results indicated recovery in the affected nerve area. This single case suggests that, in carefully selected infants who show early signs of spontaneous neurological improvement, conservative treatment may be considered as an option for managing SSEHs; however, given the limitations of a single case report, further studies are needed before this approach can be more broadly recommended.

articles.title: Evaluation of deep learning-based super-resolution reconstruction in fetal brain T2-weighted single-shot fast spin-echo imaging.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of a deep learning-based Precise IQ Engine (PIQE) in enhancing image sharpness and quality during MRI reconstruction to enhance the image quality of fetal brain single-shot fast spin-echo (SSFSE) imaging. METHODS: Fetal brain MRI scans of 14 patients, including an SSFSE sequence, acquired between January 2024 and February 2025, were analyzed. Images were reconstructed with and without PIQE (zoom ratio of 3 from low-resolution matrices). We quantified the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and image sharpness using the full width at half maximum (FWHM) of the fetal brain. Two board-certified radiologists assessed the image noise, contrast, sharpness, artifacts, and overall image quality of the two image types on a 4-point scale. We compared the quantitative and qualitative scores between the images with and without PIQE using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. RESULTS: SNRs, CNRs, and FWHM were significantly enhanced with PIQE compared to those without PIQE (SNR, CNR: p < 0.001, FWHM : p < 0.01). Qualitative scores for noise (p < 0.001), contrast (p < 0.001), sharpness (p < 0.001), artifacts (p < 0.001), and overall image quality (p < 0.001) were superior in images obtained with PIQE compared to those without it. Kappa analysis revealed moderate-to- excellent agreement for different image quality aspects: noise (κ = 0.52), contrast (κ = 0.74), sharpness (κ = 0.82), artifacts (κ = 0.61), and overall image quality (κ = 0.80). CONCLUSION: PIQE potentially enhances the image quality of fetal brain MRI using an SSFSE sequence.

articles.title: Pedicle-dural sac congruence and its relationship to pedicle dysplasia in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: A quantitative analysis using an image recognition-assisted gaussian process curve model.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To quantitatively evaluate pedicle-dural sac congruence and its relationship to pedicle dysplasia in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS). METHODS: We analyzed 64 cord-contact vertebrae (CCVs) from 52 patients with severe AIS. Using image recognition-assisted Gaussian Process (GP) curve modeling, we quantified the geometric congruence using three metrics between the pedicle wall and the dural sac on axial MRI and CT images: Procrustes disparity, Dynamic Time Warping (DTW), and Hausdorff distance. RESULTS: The concave pedicles presented significantly higher congruence with the dural sac compared to the convex pedicles across all metrics (P < 0.001). This high conformity was strongly correlated with the severity of dysplastic narrowing of the pedicle (all P < 0.001). Inter- and intra-observer agreement showed good-to-excellent reliability for all three congruency metrics, with statistical significance (all P < 0.001). The Bland-Altman plot showed a good consistency for the Procrustes disparity between MR and CT imaging modalities. CONCLUSIONS: We quantitatively validated the dysplastic concave pedicle in AIS does not merely lie adjacent to the dural sac, but conforms to its geometric contour. This congruence strongly correlates with the severity of pedicle narrowing. Therefore, our results support the hypothesis that dysplastic pedicle narrowing in AIS represents a morphological adaptation, occurring in association with spatial competition with the deviated dural sac within the rotated vertebral canal.

articles.title: Opportunistic MRI assessment of skeletal muscle mass in children and adults with Fontan circulation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Children and adults with Fontan circulation are vulnerable to reduced skeletal muscle mass because of altered Fontan physiology, exercise limitation, nutritional challenges, and chronic liver disease. Abdominal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) performed for Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD) surveillance provides an opportunity to assess muscle mass without additional imaging. OBJECTIVE: To determine the frequency of imaging-defined low skeletal muscle mass on clinically acquired abdominal MRI examinations in children and adults with Fontan circulation and, secondarily, to explore associations with available clinical and imaging markers related to FALD. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study included individuals with Fontan circulation who underwent abdominal MRI for FALD surveillance. Pediatric total psoas area and adult total skeletal muscle index were measured using age-appropriate published approaches and analyzed separately. Continuous variables were summarized with medians and interquartile ranges and explored using Spearman correlations and Mann-Whitney U tests. Sparse cardiac and outcome data were treated descriptively. RESULTS: The study included 124 individuals (78 male; 63%), including 57 children (age range 3.2-17.4 years, median=14.1) and 67 adults (age range 18.1-43.7 years, median=22.3). Imaging-defined low muscle mass was present in 17/57 children (30%) and 14/67 adults (21%) using pediatric- and adult-specific measurement approaches. Exploratory analyses did not identify a consistent pattern linking low muscle mass with the available FALD-related measures including liver stiffness measurement, liver biochemistries or liver scoring systems. Several comparisons including ejection fractions and aortopulmonary collateral flow were limited by missing data, small subgroups, and few outcome events. CONCLUSION: Clinically acquired liver MRI examinations can be repurposed to identify imaging-defined low muscle mass in individuals with Fontan circulation. The frequency observed in both age groups supports prospective evaluation of standardized MRI measurements combined with muscle function, exercise capacity, and longitudinal outcomes.

articles.title: Subperiosteal hematoma following hair braiding in a child: an unusual traction-related scalp injury.

Predictors of Clinical Outcomes Following Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt (TIPS) Placement: Comparing Baseline Liver Function Tests, Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) iterations, and the Freiburg Index of Post-TIPS Survival (FIPS).
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Accurate risk stratification is vital to optimize outcomes following Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt (TIPS) placement. This study compared the 30-day prognostic performance of traditional laboratory values, Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) iterations (MELD, MELD-Na, MELD 3.0), and the Freiburg Index of Post-TIPS Survival (FIPS). MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective study, 192 adult patients were analyzed who underwent TIPS placement from 2018 to 2024 at a US quaternary center. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite endpoint of all-cause mortality or unplanned readmission. Scoring performance was evaluated using Spearman's correlation (Rho), ANOVA with Games-Howell post hoc testing, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. RESULTS: The 30-day composite endpoint occurred in 84 patients (42%; 37 deaths, 47 readmissions). Baseline albumin, creatinine, total bilirubin, and international normalized ratio correlated with the primary outcome (all p < 0.05). Among scoring systems, MELD 3.0 showed the strongest overall correlation with the examined outcome (Rho = 0.328, p < 0.001), closely followed by FIPS (Rho = 0.310, p < 0.001). A DeLong's test found no significant difference between MELD 3.0 and FIPS in predicting short-term composite outcomes. Post hoc testing showed FIPS significantly distinguished mortality from non-readmission (p < 0.001) but not between readmissions and uneventful recoveries (p = 0.228). ROC analysis identified a FIPS threshold of 1.115 for predicting 30-day mortality, yielding 94.1% specificity, 77.2% accuracy, and 46.4% sensitivity. CONCLUSION: In this cohort, no significant difference was found between MELD 3.0 and FIPS in predicting short-term composite outcomes. MELD 3.0 offers the strongest linear tracking for short-term composite outcomes, while a FIPS score > 1.115 might serve as a highly specific tool to identify candidates at risk for early mortality.

articles.title: Does Pain Phenotype Influence Clinical Outcomes After Genicular Artery Embolization? Movement-evoked Pain Versus Pain at Rest: A Retrospective Comparative Study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Pain in knee osteoarthritis is heterogeneous and may influence clinical response to genicular artery embolization (GAE). This study aimed to compare pain reduction after GAE between patients with substantial pain at rest (SPAR) and those with predominantly movement-evoked pain (PMEP). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included patients who underwent GAE for chronic knee pain and completed follow-up evaluations at 1 and 3 months. Patients were classified as SPAR when baseline VAS pain at rest was > 3 and as PMEP when VAS pain at rest was ≤ 3. Outcomes included changes in overall VAS pain score and patient-reported clinical improvement. RESULTS: Fifty-three patients were included. Individuals with SPAR showed significantly greater overall VAS reduction than those with PMEP at both 1 month (- 4.30 ± 2.85 vs. - 2.21 ± 3.49; p = 0.023) and 3 months (- 3.68 ± 2.92 vs. - 1.68 ± 3.33; p = 0.035). On univariable regression, SPAR predicted greater 3-month VAS reduction (coefficient - 1.99; 95% CI - 3.85 to - 0.14; p = 0.035). In multivariable analysis, SPAR remained an independent predictor of pain reduction at 3 months (coefficient - 3.74; 95% CI - 6.63 to - 0.85; p = 0.014). Higher baseline WOMAC score was also independently associated with greater improvement (p = 0.004), whereas Kellgren-Lawrence grade was not significant (p = 0.187). CONCLUSION: Pain phenotype may influence response to GAE. Patients with substantial pain at rest appear to benefit more than those with predominantly movement-evoked pain, supporting phenotype-based patient selection for GAE.

articles.title: Measuring Data Leakage in the Absence of Patient Identifiers: A Public Kidney CT Benchmark and a Transferable Screen.
articles.abstract: Data leakage between training and test partitions inflates measured performance independently of a model's ability to generalise. In medical imaging its commonest form is images of one patient or acquisition in both partitions. Detecting it requires knowing which images share an origin, the field public datasets strip before release. This study measures leakage where that field is absent, in a widely used public kidney computed tomography (CT) dataset. The aim is not to restore patient identity but to recover enough of the grouping to split above the image level, and to measure what its absence has cost. A 64-bit perceptual hash read along the distributed file order resolved the 12,446 images into 219 recovered groups. These are units at the level of the acquisition, not the patient; the number of patients and their spread across groups and classes stays out of reach. Against a dataset carrying identifiers the rule divided single patients across groups more often than it merged them, so every difference reported is a lower bound. In a matched design that requires no patient identity, each of three models, trained once, scored 8.18 to 12.01 accuracy points lower on unseen groups than on seen ones, every cluster-bootstrap interval excluding zero. A nearest-neighbour rule with no learned parameters classified every test image correctly under random splitting. Of 59 studies using the dataset, two state the level at which they split. A duplicate screen applied to six further public releases returned verified overlap in three. The recovered image-to-group assignment is released.

articles.title: Impact of Documentation Aids on the Inclusion of Salient Left-Ventricular Late Gadolinium Enhancement Characteristics in Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging Impressions.
articles.abstract: Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) on cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging is a key diagnostic and prognostic biomarker in ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) and nonischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM). However, the completeness of LGE reporting in routine CMR impressions remains incompletely characterized. We aimed to evaluate the impact of large language model (LLM)-assisted reporting on the consistency of LGE pattern, distribution, and severity documentation in CMR impressions for ICM and NICM. We analyzed 828 unstructured (1990-2023) and 400 structured (2024-2025) CMR reports to identify documentation of LGE pattern, distribution, and severity. A Llama 3 language model fine-tuned on 27,000 structured CMR reports was used to generate 9650 CMR impressions; LGE attributes were extracted using an LLM judge. LLM reporting behavior was further assessed using quantized low-rank adaptation adapters trained on structured and unstructured impressions. Structured reporting captured LGE pattern more frequently than unstructured reporting overall (85.5% vs. 61.0%, p = 9.60 × 10-7) and for ICM (90.0% vs. 69.4%, p = 0.005). LLM-generated impressions demonstrated more frequent reporting of LGE distribution (75.3%) and severity (70.9%) versus structured and unstructured reports (p < 0.001). Fine-tuning with an adapter trained on unstructured impressions significantly improved reporting of all three LGE attributes. Structured reporting improved LGE pattern documentation, but gaps in LGE distribution and severity documentation persisted across human report formats. LLM-generated impressions achieved broader attribute coverage for LGE distribution and severity. Fine-tuning on unstructured data improved model performance, suggesting that passive augmentation with data capturing the documentation styles of multiple providers may help to address reporting gaps.

articles.title: MSGN: Multi-stage Self-constrained Generative Network for Orthodontic Treatment Prediction from Color Lateral Facial Photographs.
articles.abstract: People seek orthodontic treatment to improve their facial appearance. An unsolved challenge exists: how patients can visualize their post-treatment appearance before undergoing years of treatment. Existing methods that generate radiographic prediction images are not intuitive for patients. This study presents a multi-stage self-constrained generative network, MSGN, which predicts the post-treatment appearance from a single color lateral facial photograph without X-ray imaging or manual landmark tracing. MSGN detects the orthodontic change region, regresses the individualized tooth correction data, uses these data to guide post-treatment contour generation, performs photorealistic skin synthesis, and blends the result seamlessly with the untreated regions. The model was trained and evaluated on 151 patients who completed fixed-appliance extraction treatment using fivefold cross-validation, so that every patient received an independent out-of-fold prediction. The mean absolute errors were 2.16 mm for the aesthetic-line distance, 7.46   ∘  for the nasolabial angle, and 6.58   ∘  for the mentolabial angle, with a mean predicted-to-true contour point distance of 2.08 mm; all key metrics are reported with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. One case is processed in about 2 min on a standard computer. From a patient-centered perspective, MSGN therefore offers a convenient auxiliary reference that visualizes the possible post-treatment appearance to strengthen doctor-patient communication and support shared decision-making, and ongoing multi-center prospective validation will further broaden its clinical role.

articles.title: Embolization versus Nephrectomy in Hemodynamically Stable Patients with American Association for the Surgery of Trauma Grade III-V Blunt Kidney Injuries: Association with Lower Rates of Acute Kidney Injury and In-Hospital Mortality.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare rates of acute kidney injury (AKI) and in-hospital mortality between embolization and nephrectomy in hemodynamically stable patients with American Association for the Surgery of Trauma (AAST) Grade III-V blunt kidney injuries. MATERIALS AND METHODS: All cases of blunt AAST Grade III-V kidney injuries from 2017 to 2022 were identified using the American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Improvement Program database. Cases with initial hypotension (systolic blood pressure, <90 mmHg), length of stay <24 hours, nonsurvivable injuries (any abbreviated injury score of 6), and transfers were excluded. Multivariable logistic regression was utilized to assess the effect of embolization on in-hospital mortality and AKI. Inverse propensity weighting with regression adjustment was used, adjusting for gender, hospital characteristics, vital signs, Glasgow Coma Scale score, injury severity score, and grade of kidney injury. Of 849 patients, 74.4% were male, median age was 37 years (interquartile range, 24-57 years), and injury grade distribution rates were 15% Grade III, 44% Grade IV, and 41% Grade V. RESULTS: Of 849 cases of blunt AAST Grade III-V kidney injuries, 469 (55%) underwent embolization, and 380 (45%) underwent nephrectomy. On adjusted analysis, nephrectomy was associated with a 5.0% absolute increase in AKI (relative risk [RR], 2.22; P < .001) and a 7.2% absolute increase in in-hospital mortality (RR, 2.47; P < .001) compared with embolization. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that embolization is associated with both lower likelihood of AKI and mortality than nephrectomy in initially hemodynamically stable patients with blunt trauma and high-grade kidney injuries. A kidney-preservation strategy with embolization may be considered for initial management of these patients, although future prospective work is needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: MRI in Gynaecological Malignancies: Diagnostic challenges, pearls and pitfalls -A Pictorial Review.
articles.abstract: MRI plays a pivotal role in staging gynaecological malignancies owing to its superior soft tissue contrast and assessment of loco-regional disease. For accurate diagnosis and staging of gynaecological malignancies, meticulous image acquisition and skilled interpretation play a crucial role. Hormone-dependent physiological changes and associated benign lesions can pose challenges while diagnosing and/or staging malignancies. This may result in over- or under-staging of malignancies or errors in diagnosis. This pictorial essay aims to highlight the diagnostic challenges and pitfalls encountered while imaging various gynaecological malignancies on MRI. We discuss how advanced MRI sequences, such as diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), Dynamic contrast-enhanced 3D sequences (DCE), and a comprehensive interpretation of all acquired sequences, aid in overcoming these challenges. Meticulous image acquisition, multiparametric imaging, including DWI and dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences, and knowledge of likely pitfalls and tumour mimics aid in improving diagnostic accuracy while reporting gynaecological malignancies.

articles.title: Minimal Ablative Margin as a Key Predictor of Local Tumor Progression After Percutaneous Lung Tumor Ablation.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Minimally invasive local therapies such as radiofrequency ablation (RFA), microwave ablation (MWA), and cryoablation (CA) are commonly used to treat malignant lung tumors. This study aimed to identify predictors of local tumor progression (LTP), focusing on the role of minimal ablative margin. METHODS: The medical records of patients ≥ 20 years old with primary or metastatic lung tumors who underwent percutaneous ablation from July 2011 to December 2022 were retrospectively reviewed. Patient demographic information, tumor characteristics, and ablation details were extracted. The primary outcome was LTP, and the key variable of interest was the minimal ablative margin. RESULTS: Seventy-one patients with 88 nodules ablated were included in the analysis, and 22% of the nodules exhibited LTP. In the overall cohort, ROC analysis identified 3 mm as the optimal cut-off for minimal ablative margin to predict LTP. Nodules with margins ≥ 3 mm were associated with significantly higher LTP-free survival at 5 years (82% vs. 23% margins < 3 mm). Kaplan-Meier analysis indicated a significant difference in LTP between ablative margins ≥ 3 and < 3 mm (p < 0.001). RFA was associated with a higher LTP risk than MWA (hazard ratio [HR] = 5.43, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.84-16.05), as was a margin < 3 mm (HR = 24.24, 95% CI: 7.66-76.71). CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, achieving an ablative margin of at least 3 mm was associated with improved LTP-free survival after lung tumor ablation. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This threshold should be considered a pragmatic, context-dependent estimate that may require validation across ablation modalities and clinical settings.

articles.title: Spot size reduction and minibeam creation in a proton PBS nozzle using multipole permanent magnets.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Smaller spot sizes in pencil beam scanning (PBS) nozzles are generally desired to allow more conformal treatments and to spare normal tissue and organs at risk. The production of small diameter proton beams, especially proton minibeams, is challenging because long drift spaces in standard PBS nozzles exacerbate effects of MCS and finite beam divergence. PURPOSE: To investigate the use of multipole magnets in a proton PBS nozzle to create pencil beams of reduced spot size, including the creation of proton minibeams. METHODS: Monte Carlo simulations were performed in a shortened He-filled nozzle incorporating a doublet of octupole magnets and a single quadrupole magnet modeled as Halbach cylinders. Beam diameter reduction was realized by the combination of octupole tail folding and quadrupole magnetic focusing. The octupole doublet was positioned at nozzle entrance upstream of the scanning magnets and the quadrupole was (optionally) positioned at the nozzle exit. The nozzle was configured for four modes of operation, roughly described as standard pencil beam (PB mode), reduced-diameter pencil beam (PBR), symmetric minibeam (MB), and planar minibeam (MBP). Depending on nozzle mode, symmetric beam spots were produced by a continuous rotation (i.e., spinning) of the octupole doublet and the quadrupole magnet about the beam axis. Particle energies investigated covered nearly the full range typically used in clinical applications (70, 100, 150, and 225 MeV). A symmetric Gaussian beam model was used with σ = 3 mm (FWHM = 7 mm) and σ' (divergence) chosen from literature. Pencil beam and reduced diameter pencil beam dose distributions in a water phantom were compared. Minibeam composite dose distributions were created by laterally shifting single beamlet distributions in one or two dimensions, and PVDR and beamlet FWHM were determined. Modulated beams in each nozzle mode were also created. RESULTS: FWHM, FW20M, and penumbra were reduced for all PBR pencil beams compared to unshaped PB beams: at nozzle exit FWHM and FW20M were 19%-38% lower and penumbra P80/20 were 14%-59% lower, and at Bragg depth the differential full widths and penumbra were generally present; with full widths up to 21% smaller, and penumbras up to 15% smaller. The creation of single-layer planar and symmetric minibeams in MBP and MB modes showed minimum beamlet FWHM near water phantom entrance (e.g., 10 mm WED) as low as 0.7-1.4 mm and <2 mm up to a range of 3-4.5 cm of the entrance channel. PVDR was the largest for MBP beams and was as high as 910, whereas PVDR for MB beams was as high as 144. Modulated PBR penumbra were smaller compared to similar PB beams. Modulated MB and MBP minibeams produced clinically relevant PVDR. That study results were achieved ∼1 m downstream of nozzle entrance and beyond is noteworthy. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed PBS nozzle could potentially be used to produce pencil beams and modulated beams with smaller spot sizes and penumbras, including proton minibeams, suitable for clinical or preclinical applications.

articles.title: Portable ultra-low field MRI in neurocritical care and intensive care units: A systematic review of diagnostic performance and feasibility.
articles.abstract: To synthesise evidence on the diagnostic performance, safety, feasibility and clinical impact of ultra-low-field portable magnetic resonance imaging (pMRI) in adult neurocritical care and intensive care unit (ICU) populations. PubMed, Scopus and Embase were searched from inception to 6 February 2026 and supplemented by grey literature and citation searching. We included original English-language studies of adult ICU, neurocritical care or emergency department patients undergoing pMRI at ≤ 0.1 T. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Risk of bias in diagnostic comparisons was assessed with an adapted QUADAS-2 framework, and feasibility and safety outcomes were appraised narratively. Because of heterogeneity, findings were synthesised narratively. The review was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261302014). Eleven studies published between 2020 and 2024 were included, comprising 694 patient participants and 715 patient examinations, plus 40 healthy controls. Cohorts overlapped substantially: six studies came wholly and one partly from a single institution, and one ECMO study was a subset of another. The number of unique patients is therefore estimated at 281 to 677. In the multicentre ECMO study, adverse events occurred in 3 of 50 patients (6%). One was serious: an intra-aortic balloon pump malfunction attributed to electrocardiographic artefact. No adverse events were reported in the other seven independent cohorts that reported safety outcomes, and two studies did not report safety outcomes. For ischaemic stroke, pMRI detected infarction in 45 of 50 patients (90%). By sequence, sensitivity was 100% for FLAIR, 98% for T2-weighted imaging and 86% for diffusion-weighted imaging. Visual DWI-FLAIR mismatch identified patients scanned within 4.5 h with 60% sensitivity, 82% specificity and a 93% negative predictive value. Sensitivity for intracerebral haemorrhage was 80.4% (specificity 96.6%) on initial blinded evaluation. It was 92.1% (specificity 99.3%) in a later cohort in which raters had clinical context and images used deep-learning reconstruction, with lower sensitivity for infratentorial haemorrhage (75.0%). Only one subdural haemorrhage and no extradural haemorrhages were reported. Midline-shift detection showed 93% sensitivity, 96% specificity and a kappa of 0.87. pMRI detected hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury in 12 of 12 affected post-cardiac-arrest patients. In ECMO patients, pMRI detected 8 of 8 ischaemic events, compared with 4 of 8 on head CT, but only 1 of 2 haemorrhages. Up to 28% of examinations were nondiagnostic, mainly because of motion. Ultra-low-field pMRI is a feasible bedside neuroimaging adjunct with a low but non-zero adverse-event rate. It is of particular value for ischaemic injury, midline shift and serial monitoring. Lower and variable sensitivity for haemorrhage, the nonspecificity of FLAIR hyperintensity, overlapping single-institution cohorts and small samples mean that larger multicentre validation studies are needed.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence-powered solutions for environmental sustainability in medical imaging: a scoping review.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Growing evidence shows that medical imaging has a substantial environmental impact. With the increasing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in clinical settings, it is important to explore how this technology may support environmental sustainability. METHODS: Literature searches were performed across eight databases (PubMed, Wiley Online Library, Embase, Web of Science platform, the Cochrane Library, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature Ultimate, Google Scholar, and MedRxiv) for the period January 2020-June 2026. Full-text sources in the English language were eligible for inclusion. The Joanna Briggs Institute checklists were employed for risk of bias assessment. All data were analyzed using a textual narrative synthesis. RESULTS: In total, 23 studies were deemed eligible for inclusion. The literature proposed that AI tools in medical imaging could be used to minimize energy consumption by optimizing patient scheduling, decreasing scanner idle times and workstation use, reducing computed tomography over-scanning, contrast agent usage, and radiation dose, harnessing low-field magnetic resonance imaging, and curtailing low-value imaging. However, AI technologies may also impact the environment in harmful ways. CONCLUSION: Although AI-powered solutions hold promise for improving sustainability in medical imaging, the true environmental impact remains largely unexplored. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: The findings of this work further strengthen the dual role of AI adoption in medical imaging related to environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Reconfigurable liquid-based acoustic lens for controlling the focal depth of focused ultrasound.
articles.abstract: Focused ultrasound (FUS) enables noninvasive treatment. Conventional FUS transducers with fixed geometries lack depth control, whereas dynamic focusing with multi-element phased arrays requires complex electronics that limit scalability. This study introduces a reconfigurable, liquid-based acoustic lens that attaches to a single-element planar ultrasound transducer to provide tunable focal-depth control. The lens consisted of a deformable low-density polyethylene membrane filled with perfluorooctyl bromide (PFOB), a biocompatible liquid with matching acoustic impedance and low reflectivity, and was coupled to a 500-kHz transducer. Adjusting the internal PFOB volume changed the lens curvature and acoustic wavefront, thereby controlling focal depth. Acoustic pressure fields were mapped under three conditions: no lens, 2 mL PFOB, and 3 mL PFOB. Cross-sectional analysis showed volume-dependent plano-convex lens deformation, with central heights of approximately 3.6 mm and 4.7 mm at 2 mL and 3 mL, respectively. Acoustic field maps showed that increasing the PFOB volume shortened the focal depth from 52 mm without a lens to 37 mm and 26 mm, with improved focal localization. Numerical simulations closely reproduced the experimental pressure maps. These findings demonstrate controllable focusing with a reconfigurable, liquid-based acoustic lens in a compact, single-element FUS system.

articles.title: Estimating magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction from ultrasound attenuation and clinical parameters in pediatric hepatic steatosis: development of a prediction model.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the ultrasound-guided attenuation parameter (UGAP) for pediatric hepatic steatosis and developed a multivariable model to estimate magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) from ultrasound and clinical variables. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included pediatric patients who underwent UGAP measurement and MRI-PDFF assessment within 3 months of each other. UGAP performance in detecting moderate-to-severe (≥S2) and severe (S3) steatosis was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Multivariable models were developed using linear regression and a random forest algorithm with five-fold cross-validation. RESULTS: Among 45 patients (33 male and 12 female; median age, 12 years), median UGAP and MRI-PDFF values were 0.83 dB/cm/MHz and 22%, respectively. UGAP correlated moderately with MRI-PDFF (ρ=0.596, P<0.001). The AUC was 0.74 for both ≥S2 and S3 steatosis (95% confidence intervals [CIs], 0.58 to 0.91 and 0.60 to 0.89, respectively), and two discordant cases were identified. A model incorporating UGAP, age, height, and liver size outperformed UGAP alone in detecting ≥S2 steatosis (optimism-corrected AUC, 0.882 vs. 0.744; P=0.01). In the machine learning analysis, the model showed stable performance during cross-validation, with an AUC of 0.789 (95% CI, 0.649 to 0.928) for ≥S2 steatosis and an R² of 0.663 for continuous MRI-PDFF prediction. CONCLUSION: UGAP correlated moderately with MRI-PDFF and showed fair performance in grading pediatric hepatic steatosis. Combining UGAP with clinical parameters significantly improved MRI-PDFF estimation, providing a practical screening tool for hepatic steatosis when MRI is unavailable. External validation is needed.

articles.title: Shear wave elastography in infantile fibromatosis colli: associations with clinical severity and short-term outcomes.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study evaluated shear wave elastography (SWE) in infants with fibromatosis colli by assessing the associations of ultrasonography (US) and SWE with clinical severity and outcomes. METHODS: This retrospective study included infants with fibromatosis colli who underwent US with SWE between June 2019 and December 2021. Lesion size and longitudinal extent of sternocleidomastoid involvement were measured, with extent categorized using a four-point scale (<25%, 25%-49%, 50%-74%, and ≥75%). SWE parameters included mean and median elasticity and the elasticity ratio (E-ratio; mass/normal muscle). Clinical severity was classified as mild or severe and 3-month outcomes as improved or non-improved. Associations of imaging parameters with clinical severity and outcomes were analyzed. RESULTS: Thirty-five infants (mean age, 1.1±1.4 months; 19 male infants) were included; 21 had mild and 14 severe disease. Of these, 29 underwent approximately 3-month follow-up, with 16 classified as improved and 13 as non-improved. Baseline extent scores and E-ratios were higher in the severe group (P=0.009 and P=0.004, respectively) and correlated with clinical severity (r=0.50, P=0.002; r=0.41, P=0.016, respectively). The non-improved group had higher baseline mean and median elasticity (24.35/23.70 vs. 18.02/16.61 kPa, P=0.037/P=0.032) and a higher E-ratio (3.09 vs. 1.90, P=0.002). The E-ratio had an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.81 and remained associated with non-improvement after age adjustment (odds ratio, 3.73; 95% confidence interval, 1.57 to 12.29; P=0.009). CONCLUSION: In infantile fibromatosis colli, longitudinal extent and E-ratio were associated with baseline clinical severity. SWE-derived stiffness measures, particularly E-ratio, were associated with short-term outcomes.

articles.title: Serial ultrasonographic monitoring during defibrotide treatment of sinusoidal obstruction syndrome after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a longitudinal study of treatment response.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study evaluated serial ultrasonographic (US) changes during defibrotide therapy for sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (SOS) after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, identifying parameters whose temporal trajectories differed by treatment response. METHODS: This retrospective study included adults treated with defibrotide for SOS between January 2015 and August 2024 with baseline US and at least one follow-up US examination. Response was defined a priori as total bilirubin <2 mg/dL with resolution of SOS-related multiorgan dysfunction. US was repeated weekly until response assessment. HokUS-10 parameters and additional US findings were analyzed using generalized estimating equations and linear mixed-effects models to test the group-by-time interaction. The fully adjusted model was primary, with a minimal model used for sensitivity analysis. P-values were adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. RESULTS: Among 39 patients (23 responders [59.0%] and 16 non-responders [41.0%]; median defibrotide duration, 23 days), only HokUS-10 score showed a significant group-by-time interaction after multiple-testing adjustment in both models, declining more rapidly among responders (fully adjusted model: β=-0.048; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.083 to -0.013; P=0.017; minimal model: β=-0.053; 95% CI, -0.087 to -0.019; P=0.006). The odds of hepatofugal portal vein flow decreased faster among responders in the fully adjusted model (odds ratio [OR], 0.92; 95% CI, 0.85 to 0.99; P=0.032), whereas the association was directionally similar but non-significant in the minimal model (OR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.88 to 1.02; P=0.162). Hepatic artery resistive index ≥0.75 was not significantly associated with differential temporal change. CONCLUSION: Serial US trajectories differed by treatment response. Longitudinal HokUS-10 changes may help distinguish defibrotide responders from non-responders.

articles.title: Microflow imaging versus color Doppler imaging for differentiating malignant from non-neoplastic peripheral lung lesions.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to compare microflow imaging (MFI) with conventional color Doppler imaging (CDI) for differentiating malignant from non-neoplastic peripheral lung lesions on the basis of vascular grading and vascular morphology. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 124 patients with pleura-based peripheral lung lesions who underwent thoracic ultrasound between January 2024 and January 2026. Each lesion was examined with B-mode ultrasound, CDI, and MFI during the same session. Vascularity was graded according to the Adler classification, and vascular morphology was assigned to one of five predefined patterns. Histopathological findings or clinical and radiological follow-up served as the reference standard. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis and multivariable logistic regression were performed. RESULTS: Among the 124 lesions, 77 (62.1%) were malignant and 47 (37.9%) were non-neoplastic. Vascularity scores obtained with both MFI and CDI were significantly higher in malignant lesions than in non-neoplastic lesions (P<0.001). The MFI morphology score achieved the highest diagnostic performance (area under the curve [AUC], 0.933; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.888 to 0.979), followed by the MFI Adler score (AUC, 0.899), CDI Adler score (AUC, 0.847), and CDI morphology score (AUC, 0.828). At a cutoff of ≥3, the MFI morphology score yielded 94% sensitivity and 83% specificity. In multivariable analysis, only the MFI morphology score remained an independent predictor of malignancy (odds ratio, 6.13; 95% CI, 2.02 to 18.56; P=0.001). CONCLUSION: MFI, particularly vascular morphology assessment, showed better diagnostic performance than CDI for differentiating malignant from non-neoplastic peripheral lung lesions and may improve routine thoracic ultrasound evaluation.

articles.title: Multi-positional ultrasonographic assessment of clinically suspected pediatric nutcracker syndrome.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to characterize position-dependent variations in the left renal vein (LRV) in children with suspected nutcracker syndrome (NCS) across supine, standing, and bilateral lateral decubitus positions. METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 67 children with clinically suspected NCS, with a median age of 10.0 years. LRV diameters were measured in the supine, standing, left lateral decubitus (LLD), and right lateral decubitus (RLD) positions, and peak systolic velocities were measured in the supine and standing positions. Diameter ratios (hilar/stenotic) were calculated, and the associations of demographic and clinical characteristics with position-dependent anatomical changes were analyzed. RESULTS: The median diameter ratio was highest in the supine position (4.4). Compared with the supine baseline, the diameter ratio decreased significantly in the LLD (3.3) and RLD (3.1) positions (both P<0.001), whereas the decrease in the standing position (4.0) was not statistically significant. Velocity and diameter ratios were positively correlated in both the supine (Spearman rho=0.539, P<0.001) and standing positions (Spearman rho=0.432, P<0.001). Lateral positioning reduced the prevalence of abnormal diameter ratios (>4.0) from 62.7% in the supine position to 31.3% in the LLD position and 23.9% in the RLD position, with no significant difference between the two lateral positions. Male patients had a significantly greater reduction in diameter ratio in the RLD position than female patients (P=0.021). CONCLUSION: Lateral decubitus positioning provided significant anatomical alleviation of LRV compression compared with the supine baseline in children with clinically suspected NCS. The LLD and RLD positions provided comparable morphological decompression. Comprehensive multi-positional assessment is needed to capture dynamic LRV variation and may provide an objective anatomical basis for considering postural adjustments during conservative observation.

articles.title: Carotid intima thickness assessed using high-resolution ultrasound as a structural correlate of endothelial dysfunction.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study evaluated the association between carotid intima thickness (cIT), measured using high-resolution ultrasound, and endothelial cell dysfunction (ECD), assessed using flow-mediated dilation (FMD), for early atherosclerosis risk assessment. METHODS: Between January and December 2024, 102 middle-aged nonsmoking participants were prospectively recruited; 66 were included in the final analysis and classified into a risk group (n=44) or control group (n=22) according to the presence or absence of at least one conventional cardiovascular risk factor. Data collected included demographic characteristics, physical measurements, laboratory findings, cIT, carotid media thickness (cMT), and carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT). After 5 minutes of forearm occlusion, brachial artery diameters were measured at baseline and at 30, 60, and 120 seconds after cuff deflation during systole and diastole, and FMD indices were calculated. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed, with differences between the ROC curves evaluated using the Hanley-McNeil test. RESULTS: Compared with the control group, the risk group had greater cIT (P<0.001) and cIMT (P=0.016) and generally lower FMD indices. cMT did not differ significantly between groups (P=0.595). Among carotid ultrasound parameters, cIT showed the strongest association with atherosclerosis risk (standardized β=0.489, P<0.05) and the strongest inverse correlation with systolic FMD measured 60 seconds after cuff deflation (FMDS60; ρ=-0.689, adjusted P=0.001). In ROC analysis, cIT generally showed better performance for identifying ECD than cMT and cIMT, with a maximum area under the curve of 0.896 (P<0.001). CONCLUSION: High-resolution ultrasound measurement of cIT may provide a noninvasive imaging marker of early endothelial dysfunction.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided thermal ablation for T1b and selected T2 papillary thyroid carcinoma: current evidence, evolving guideline recommendations, and an ultrasound-based clinical workflow.
articles.abstract: Thermal ablation (TA) is established for benign thyroid nodules, recurrent thyroid carcinoma, and low-risk papillary thyroid microcarcinoma. Its role in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) remains unsettled. This review examines evidence and guideline recommendations for TA in T1b and selected T2 PTC. T1b studies suggest encouraging local control and low permanent morbidity, but retrospective, geographically concentrated, heterogeneous evidence leaves surgery as the reference treatment. Four retrospective T2 reports indicate a narrower procedural safety margin. The same anatomical selection criteria apply across T1a, T1b, and T2 disease; however, as tumors enlarge, fewer patients meet oncological and technical requirements, and incomplete staging or margins have greater consequences.

articles.title: Assessing the repeatability and accuracy of quantitative double-echo steady-state (qDESS) as a wT2-mapping technique in test objects and the lower limb of healthy volunteers.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: A multiple-echo spin-echo (MESE) acquisition is conventional for T2-mapping of skeletal muscle. Its time-intensive nature can make it impractically long for muscular dystrophies (MDs) such as facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD). Here we assess the feasibility of using 3D quantitative double-echo steady-state (qDESS) to quantify muscle-water T2 (wT2) by evaluating the repeatability and accuracy of the estimated wT2 values. METHODS: First, the precision of qDESS as a wT2-mapping technique was determined by comparing against MESE and stimulated echo acquisition mode (STEAM) wT2 values from a phantom of eight MnCl2-doped water phantoms with concentrations ranging from 0.1-0.45 mM in 0.05 mM increments. Then, test-retest qDESS muscle-water wT2 maps of six lower limb muscles from eight healthy volunteers underwent a Bland-Altman analysis to assess repeatability. qDESS- and MESE-derived wT2 values were assessed against STEAM wT2 values at matched locations along the gastrocnemius medialis of a further five healthy volunteers to assess and compare accuracy. RESULTS: qDESS showed good repeatability and strong agreement with STEAM in test objects and the lower limb. CONCLUSION: 3D qDESS produces repeatable and accurate wT2 maps of the lower limb with substantially shorter acquisition times than the MESE sequence, making it a viable tool for clinical trials of MDs.

articles.title: Acute fractures and mimics in adult musculoskeletal radiographs.
articles.abstract: Radiographs are the first line imaging modality in evaluation for fractures, which can be challenging in equivocal cases with findings that mimic fractures. Accurate and quick identification of acute fractures is essential for triage, management, and prevention of complications. At the same time, overcalling a benign finding as a fracture can lead to patient anxiety and further testing that adds health care cost and time. As such, familiarity with fracture mimics is a critical skill for clinicians involved in emergency and acute care settings. This pictorial essay reviews common acute fracture patterns and highlights key imaging features that distinguish acute fractures from benign mimics, primarily through numerous representative cases. The article also provides a framework to address equivocal findings with next steps that can be performed for troubleshooting.

Multimodal Photoacoustic/Ultrasound Imaging System for Longitudinal Assessment of Keloid Treatment.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility of using a multimodal photoacoustic/ultrasound imaging system for longitudinal monitoring of keloid lesions during intralesional therapy, and to assess its potential as an objective tool for treatment follow-up. METHODS: A patient with 5 keloids underwent serial imaging at 5 time points during intralesional injections of betamethasone and 5-fluorouracil. Clinical assessment was performed using the Vancouver Scar Scale (VSS). A multimodal photoacoustic/ultrasound imaging system which integrates different techniques was used to monitor structural, vascular, oxygenation, and elasticity changes during treatment. Structural parameters were assessed by grayscale ultrasound (GSUS), vascularity was evaluated by ultrasonographic microvascular angiography (UMA) and photoacoustic imaging (PAI), while oxygen saturation (SO2) provided by PAI, and elasticity was measured via elastography. RESULTS: VSS scores decreased significantly from 7.6 ± 2.3 at baseline to 2.2 ± 1.6 at T4 (p = .001), with improvements in pigmentation (p = .003), pliability (p = .009), and vascularity (p = .004). GSUS showed a reduction in total lesion thickness from 26.8 ± 10.5 mm to 8.0 ± 4.5 mm (p = .006), along with significant decreases in lesion lengths (p < .05). PAI demonstrated a decline in blood flow signals and an increase in SO2 levels in most lesions. UMA and PAI revealed reduced vascular density during treatment. Early-stage increases in stiffness were observed, but subsequent measurements became unfeasible as the lesions thinned. CONCLUSION: A multimodal PA/US imaging system provides comprehensive and noninvasive assessment of both structural and functional changes in keloids during treatment. This longitudinal study suggests its potential as a valuable tool for objective and dynamic monitoring of therapeutic response in scar management.
